author: TheFlowerShow
name: Flower Show
text:
Protecting flowers from frost in ice ?!?

Yes ! This method is a bit confusing but there is method to the madness:

When water freezes and turns into ice, it actually releases a bunch of warmth, called latent heat of fusion (roughly 144 BTUs per pound of water).

So here’s the magic: as long as you keep gently spraying a thin layer of water that’s constantly freezing on the plants, that freezing process keeps releasing heat. 

This holds the temperature of the plant tissues right around 32°F (0°C), the freezing point, instead of letting them drop colder and get damaged.

The ice coat looks dramatic and acts like a protective shell, but the real hero is the ongoing freezing of the fresh water, not the ice itself. It’s like giving your flowers a cozy, self-warming blanket all night long!

The only thing you need to consider is the weight of the ice !

Video is from a nursery that actively uses this method to protect there plants.
